body.statement:
For every fixed \(c>0\), every probability vector \(P\in\Delta^{15}\), and every real \(\Delta\), including laws with zero cells, one has
\[
 (\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_{\mathrm w}(P)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \mathcal F_c^{\mathrm w}(P,\Delta)\ne\varnothing,
 \qquad
 (\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_+(P)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \mathcal F_c^+(P,\Delta)\ne\varnothing. \tag{1}
\]
The forward map forms the eight joint response-type measures
\(d\nu_{(x,r_0,r_1)}=h_xg_{x0}(r_0,\cdot)g_{x1}(r_1,\cdot)d\mu\), then sets \(d\rho_s=D_c^{-1}d\nu_s\) and records the five moments through degree four.  The reverse map takes positive-half-line representing measures, sets \(d\nu_s=D_c\,d\rho_s\), and reconstructs one probability law and legal sequential initial and feedback kernels by Radon--Nikodym derivatives.  For the strict class, the \(6\times6\) blocks give a common positive-node representation with every type weight positive, which makes every reconstructed initial and feedback probability strictly positive almost everywhere.  The weak lift uses exactly fifty-six scalar variables, eight \(3\times3\) PSD blocks, and eight \(4\times4\) PSD blocks; the strict lift uses sixty-four variables and eight additional \(6\times6\) PSD blocks.  Thus (1) is equality with the independently model-defined fibers, not an outer bound, and no cellwise-positivity condition on \(P\) is required.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(c>0\), \(P\in\Delta^{15}\), and \(\Delta\in\mathbb R\).  All changes of measure below are legal because
\[
 D_c(u)=(1+u)^2(1+cu)^2>0
 \qquad(u>0). \tag{2}
\]
The sequential response restriction is used through the history-conditioned factorization
\[
 \Pr(Y_1=y,X_2=z,Y_2=w\mid X_1=x,u)
 =p_x(y,u)g_{xy}(z,u)p_z(w,u), \tag{3}
\]
which follows by multiplying the first-period response kernel, the feedback kernel, and the second-period response kernel conditional on the full realized history.  Equation (3) invokes no conditional independence beyond those declared sequential kernels.

Start with \((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\) generating \(P\) and \(\Delta\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}response\text{-}measure\text{-}equivalence}\), the joint response construction gives eight nonnegative finite measures \(\nu_s\) whose sum is the probability measure \(\mu\), and
\[
 P(x,y,z,w)=\sum_{r:r_y=z}\int p_x(y,u)p_z(w,u)\,d\nu_{(x,r)}(u),
 \qquad
 \Delta=\sum_{s\in S}\int\frac{(c-1)u}{(1+u)(1+cu)}\,d\nu_s(u). \tag{4}
\]
Define \(d\rho_s=D_c^{-1}d\nu_s\).  For \(0\le k\le4\), the function \(u^k/D_c(u)\) is bounded on \((0,\infty)\): it has a finite limit as \(u\downarrow0\), is continuous on every compact positive interval, and is of order \(u^{k-4}\) as \(u\to\infty\).  Hence all \(m_{s,k}=\int u^k d\rho_s\) are finite.  Direct substitution of the binary-logit probabilities yields
\[
 D_c(u)p_x(y,u)p_z(w,u)
 =c^{xy+zw}u^{y+w}(1+u)^{x+z}(1+cu)^{2-x-z}
 =A_{xz,yw}(u), \tag{5}
\]
and
\[
 D_c(u)\frac{(c-1)u}{(1+u)(1+cu)}
 =(c-1)u(1+u)(1+cu)=N_c(u). \tag{6}
\]
Both right sides have degree at most four.  Therefore (4) is exactly
\[
 P(x,y,z,w)=\sum_{r:r_y=z}L_{m_{(x,r)}}(A_{xz,yw}),
 \qquad
 \Delta=\sum_{s\in S}L_{m_s}(N_c). \tag{7}
\]
For each type, \(\mathrm{lem{:}open\text{-}stieltjes\text{-}quartic}\) supplies \(a_s,b_s\) for which \(H_s\succeq0\) and \(K_s\succeq0\).  Equations (7) and \(\mathrm{def{:}weak\text{-}lift}\) prove weak lifted feasibility.

If the original model is strict, then for every \(s=(x,r_0,r_1)\),
\[
 h_x(u)g_{x0}(r_0,u)g_{x1}(r_1,u)>0
 \quad\text{for }\mu\text{-almost every }u. \tag{8}
\]
Thus every \(\nu_s\), and then every \(\rho_s\) by (2), is mutually absolutely continuous with \(\mu\).  For \(v=(v_0,v_1,v_2)^{\mathsf T}\), put \(q_v(u)=v_0+v_1u+v_2u^2\).  The identity
\[
 v^{\mathsf T}H_sv=\int q_v(u)^2\,d\rho_s(u) \tag{9}
\]
shows that all \(H_s\) have the same null space and hence the same range.  Because the null space of a sum of positive-semidefinite matrices is the intersection of their null spaces, \(H_\Sigma\) has this same range.  Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}generalized\text{-}schur\text{-}range}\) with \(A=H_s\) and \(B=H_\Sigma\) supplies a finite \(t_s\) such that \(R_s\succeq0\).  This proves strict lifted feasibility.

Conversely, suppose \((m,a,b)\in\mathcal F_c^{\mathrm w}(P,\Delta)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}open\text{-}stieltjes\text{-}quartic}\), choose for each type a finite nonnegative measure \(\rho_s\) on \((0,\infty)\) representing \(m_{s,0},\ldots,m_{s,4}\), and set
\[
 d\nu_s(u)=D_c(u)\,d\rho_s(u). \tag{10}
\]
These measures are finite because \(D_c\) has degree four and the five represented moments are finite.  Summing all sixteen cell equations in (7), for each fixed \(s=(x,r)\) the restriction \(r_y=z\) selects one \(z\) for each \(y\).  The normalizations \(\sum_y p_x(y,u)=1\) and \(\sum_w p_{r_y}(w,u)=1\) therefore imply, equivalently by (5), that the polynomial summed for type \(s\) is \(D_c\).  Since \(P\in\Delta^{15}\),
\[
 1=\sum_{x,y,z,w}P(x,y,z,w)
 =\sum_{s\in S}L_{m_s}(D_c)
 =\sum_{s\in S}\nu_s((0,\infty)). \tag{11}
\]
No cellwise lower bound was used.  Equations (5)--(7) show that the path and APE integrals of \(\nu\) equal exactly \(P\) and \(\Delta\).  The reverse direction of \(\mathrm{lem{:}response\text{-}measure\text{-}equivalence}\) now sets \(\mu=\sum_s\nu_s\) and reconstructs normalized measurable kernels \(h\) and \(g\), yielding an element of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\) which, by the sequential factorization (3), generates exactly the stipulated law and APE.  Types of zero mass cause no problem: the Radon--Nikodym construction assigns arbitrary probability-vector versions on their null sets.

For the strict converse, let \((m,a,b,t)\in\mathcal F_c^+(P,\Delta)\).  The generalized Schur range criterion applied to \(R_s\succeq0\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Range}(H_\Sigma)\subseteq\operatorname{Range}(H_s)
 \quad(s\in S). \tag{12}
\]
Since \(H_\Sigma-H_s=\sum_{j\ne s}H_j\succeq0\), one has \(\ker H_\Sigma\subseteq\ker H_s\); symmetry gives
\(\operatorname{Range}(H_s)\subseteq\operatorname{Range}(H_\Sigma)\).  Hence all ranges in (12) are equal.  If some \(H_s=0\), (12) forces \(H_\Sigma=0\).  Positivity of every summand then forces every \(H_j=0\), and the Hankel entries give \(m_{j,k}=0\) for all \(j\) and \(0\le k\le4\).  This contradicts the normalization (11).  Thus every \(m_s\ne0\).

All hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}positive\text{-}support}\) are now satisfied.  Choose finite representing measures \(\rho_s\) on one finite set \(Q\subset(0,\infty)\), with every \(\rho_s\) assigning strictly positive mass to every node of \(Q\).  By (2), multiplication by \(D_c\) preserves every positive type weight in (10).  At each \(q\in Q\), the Radon--Nikodym reconstruction is the elementary ratio
\[
 h_x(q)=
 \frac{\sum_{r\in B^2}\nu_{(x,r)}(\{q\})}
      {\sum_{j\in S}\nu_j(\{q\})}>0, \tag{13}
\]
and, for all \(x,y,z\in B\),
\[
 g_{xy}(z,q)=
 \frac{\sum_{r:r_y=z}\nu_{(x,r)}(\{q\})}
      {\sum_{r\in B^2}\nu_{(x,r)}(\{q\})}>0. \tag{14}
\]
Every denominator in (13)--(14) is positive because every type has positive weight at every node.  Since \(\mu=\sum_s\nu_s\) is concentrated on \(Q\), (13)--(14) prove strict initial assignment and strict feedback \(\mu\)-almost everywhere.  The reconstructed model is therefore in \(\mathcal M_+(c)\) and generates exactly \(P\) and \(\Delta\).

Finally, \(m\) has \(8\cdot5=40\) coordinates and \((a,b)\) has sixteen, giving fifty-six weak variables.  There are eight blocks \(H_s\in\mathbb S^3\) and eight blocks \(K_s\in\mathbb S^4\).  The strict lift adds eight coordinates \(t_s\) and eight blocks \(R_s\in\mathbb S^6\), giving sixty-four variables.  The forward and reverse constructions prove both equivalences in (1), including singular and zero-type weak cases, so the representation is sharp rather than merely an outer bound.
body.justification: Normalization of the lifted response measures uses only \(P\in\Delta^{15}\), so the legal-kernel reconstruction remains exact with zero observed cells and zero weak type measures.
body.gap: Positive observed cells were previously carried as an unnecessary premise of the cone equivalence rather than isolated to the positive-margin comparator translation.
body.consumer: The all-laws theorem makes the finite certificate usable on boundary observed laws without pretending that endpoint continuity or uniform boundary inference follows.
